_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for risk classification. /ai-task reads this file to decide which stages are mandatory, which model tier plans and reviews the change, whether a human must approve before anything leaves the branch, and — through pipeline_profile — which stages the main session does inline and which go to a subagent. The tier comes from the SCOPE of a change — what it reaches: a migration, a process whose behaviour changes, money, identity, infrastructure — never from how many files or lines it touches; the diff budget below measures size and reports it, it does not classify. risk-tiers.md is a human-readable mirror of this file; when they disagree, this file wins. Adjust the triggers to the project after /ai-init — the defaults are generic.

pipeline_profiles._comment: WHO runs a stage, not WHETHER it runs: stages_required is fixed per tier, the profile decides which of them are delegated to a subagent and which the main session does inline in a few lines. 'solo' is for one developer who knows the codebase and has two modes. DIRECT (T0–T4): no pipeline ceremony — the session names the files, edits, runs each step's own scoped tests, then the verification command once at the end and the e2e suite once after it, fixing every failure as one batch; the only subagents are cheap readers (Explore, log-reader), one BALANCED review at T2/T3 when a sensor is red, and at T4 — where the plan is written in plan mode and approved by the human — one review on STRONG. SDLC (T5–T6): the full pipeline with delegated plan, plan review, adversarial review, security review and release report, on the STRONG and EXPERT tiers. 'team' is the fully delegated pipeline. Switch by editing pipeline_profile.

delegate_anyway_when: the developer says the area is unfamiliar, or the request names no entry point and grep does not find one within a few calls (Explore on FAST, then ai-discovery if Explore returned nothing usable)
the inline context summary has an UNKNOWN the plan depends on (ai-discovery, one agent)
the risk tier is T4 or above and not obvious from the trigger table (ai-risk on STRONG)
the verification command prints more than ~40 lines (log-reader on FAST), or the test setup is unfamiliar (ai-tester on FAST)
at T4, the change crosses a module the developer does not own, or plan mode leaves a (blocking) question open (ai-planner on STRONG, one call)
solo.release_report: T0–T3: the commit message body; T4: the same short form, also appended to task.md; T5 and T6: ai-release

plan.T2: three to five lines in the conversation, registered through `state.py quick`
plan.T3: three to five lines in the conversation — the files of the resource and its screens — registered through `state.py quick`; plan mode only when the change spans several modules
plan.T4: the session, in plan mode: numbered steps with their files, the characterization tests first, a one-line rollback; the human accepting plan mode is the plan approval, then `state.py quick --tier T4`
plan.T5: ai-planner on STRONG, in plan mode

solo.test: three scopes. During a step: only the tests the plan named for that step (`step_test_command` scoped to its files), fixed inside the step before `state.py step-done` — never the full suite, never e2e. After the LAST step: `verify_command` once, to the end, no fail-fast flag, output through tail -40 or log-reader; every failure is collected and classified first, every NEW REGRESSION is fixed in ONE `state.py remediate` step and the command runs once more, at most two rounds. At the END of the task, after the full suite is green: `e2e_command` once, never per step, skipped at T0/T1 and when no e2e-covered flow can be reached (say which).
solo.e2e: once per task, at the end, after verify_command is green and before the adversarial review. T0/T1: none. T2+: required when the change can reach a flow the e2e suite covers, otherwise one line saying why it cannot. T5/T6: always, and its result goes in the release report. Record it with `state.py set e2e_status <passing|failing|not_applicable|not_run>`.
solo.triage: T0/T1: no state file. T2, T3 and T4: `state.py quick` records discovery, context, impact, risk and the one-step plan in a single call (at T4 after the human approved the plan). T5+: the stages run and are recorded one at a time.

artifacts.T2: none — the state archive and the commit message
artifacts.T3: none — the state archive and the commit message
artifacts.T4: task.md with the plan, the review verdict and the release short form

direct.state: T0/T1: none — the commit message is the record. T2–T4: one `state.py quick` call (init + triage + one-step plan) so the scope guard is armed; `state.py close` at the end (T4: after the human approved the result)
direct.plan: T0/T1: say which files, in one line. T2/T3: three to five lines in the conversation — steps and files — never a file. T4: the same list written in plan mode, with characterization tests first and a rollback line; the human approves it before any edit
direct.agents: Explore and log-reader on FAST for reading; ai-implementer on BALANCED for a mechanical pattern-copy step; ai-reviewer on BALANCED at T2/T3 only when `state.py review-gate` says the review is required, and on STRONG once at T4 — no ai-planner, no plan-review agent, no ai-release
direct.review: T0/T1: none. T2/T3: `state.py review-gate` first — every sensor green is the review (`skipped_green`); otherwise one ai-reviewer on the BALANCED model over the diff, after the tests pass. T4: one ai-reviewer on STRONG after review-gate, plus ai-security only when auth, authorization or personal data is touched. Findings fixed as one batch in a `state.py remediate` step; one scoped re-review only when a BLOCKER was fixed
direct.release: the commit message body: what changed, verification command and result, rollback

team.test: step-scoped tests inside each step (`step_test_command`, the tests the plan named for that step); ai-tester once after the last step on `verify_command`, to the end with no fail-fast flag; every failure is fixed as one batch in a `state.py remediate` step, then one more run
team.e2e: ai-tester once at the end of the task on `e2e_command`, after verify_command is green; never inside a step

tiers._comment: Seven tiers, by scope. T0–T3 add or present; T4 changes a process; T5 touches money, identity or customer data; T6 is irreversible. The heavy gates — a delegated plan and its review, the security review, the full release report — start at T5.

T0.label: documentation only
T0.plan: none — say which files you will touch, then edit

T1.label: isolated presentation tweak
examples: a label or a small presentation tweak
a template or stylesheet change with no logic
T1.plan: none — say which files you will touch, then edit

T2.label: isolated screen or small feature
examples: an isolated admin screen or form
a new field on an existing form, a grid column or filter
a small isolated feature that changes no existing process
this repository: a change that moves no guard decision and no state.py refusal — skill or agent text, usage-report, installer paths, performance work that keeps the guard golden byte-identical
T2.adversarial_review: the sensors, with the named tests proven to bite; one BALANCED model review only when a sensor is red
T2.plan: a short numbered list of steps with their files, inline

T3.label: CRUD and presentation
examples: a new resource: entity, repository, form, grid, routes, menu, translations
a new service with limited blast radius
anything that adds and presents data without changing an existing process
this repository: a change that adds a decision or a refusal — a new deny, a new sensor, a new state.py check — or changes a deny's reason text, the guard golden re-recorded
T3.adversarial_review: the sensors, with the named tests proven to bite; one BALANCED model review only when a sensor is red
T3.plan: a short numbered list of steps with their files, inline — no characterization tests, no STRONG review: this tier adds, it does not change a process

T4.label: shared domain behaviour and processes
examples: a schema migration that adds to an existing table

this repository: a change that allows what was denied or weakens a refusal; one that changes the approval path (approve, questions --sync, AI_UNATTENDED, review_status transitions); one that changes how user projects are installed or migrated (install.sh, the project-update merge, tools/)
T4.security_review: when the change touches authentication, authorization or personal data
T4.plan: plan mode in the session; the human approves the plan before implementation

T5.label: critical business or system behaviour
extra_requirements: idempotency and retry behaviour must be stated explicitly

T6.label: system level, irreversible, production architecture
extra_requirements: migration analysis: locks, table size, duration, deployment ordering, old-version compatibility
a rehearsed rollback plan, not a described one
destructive operations need explicit, separate human approval naming the operation

LOCAL.note: No local model runs inside Claude Code or Codex. The work this tier would do — indexing, listing, counting, summarising git history — is done by deterministic tools (rg, git, jq, the framework CLI) and by ai-indexer on the cheapest model.

FAST.note: readers and runners: they collect, run and report; anything they cannot settle is escalated one tier, never retried on the same one

BALANCED.agent: ai-discovery, ai-context, ai-risk, ai-planner, ai-release, ai-implementer; ai-reviewer at T2 and T3
BALANCED.effort: low for compression and mechanical edits, medium for judgement
BALANCED.note: the default tier for agents; the main session runs the installed profile's model and does the implementation itself

STRONG.agent: ai-reviewer from T4, ai-security; ai-planner and ai-risk on STRONG (under Codex the ai-planner-strong and ai-risk-strong agents, because a Codex agent file outranks a spawn-time model)

EXPERT.agent: ai-expert; architect for design outside a task

diff_budget._comment: A per-tier ceiling on what one step and one task may change, measured by skills/ai-task/sensors.py between two tree objects. ADVISORY unless `enforce` is true: over the budget, state.py step-done finishes the step and prints a warning that names step-split, and the re-score records `over_budget` without raising the tier — the tier comes from the scope of a change (path_scopes and the trigger table), never from its size. Advisory never means unread: a task over its budget cannot close on skipped_green, a reviewer reads it. With `enforce: true` the old behaviour returns: step-done exits 6 and a task over its budget is re-scored one tier up. lines = added + deleted after `exclude` and `unbudgeted_scopes`. The numbers sit near the band where a review still finds defects (a few hundred lines); T3/T4 are wider because a resource and its screens, or shared-domain work and its callers, legitimately span many files; T5/T6 are tighter because those reviews read every line. Adjust them to the project and calibrate from /usage-report.

_path_scopes_comment: Ordered, first match wins per file — that is why `pipeline` stands above `docs` (an instruction file is pipeline, not documentation), `dependencies` above `docs` (requirements.txt is a manifest, not a text file) and `tests` above `payments` (a test for the payment code is a test). A file matching nothing is scope `source` and demands no tier. min_tier is the lowest tier a change touching that scope may have, and every floor that changes a process — pipeline, dependencies, migrations, config — is T4, above the ceiling at which the sensors may stand in for a reader: a migration file is T4 at least (it changes a process, even when it only adds a table — a destructive or data migration is T6 by the trigger table), money and identity are T5, infrastructure is T6. state.py step-done re-scores the task from the real diff and raises the tier when it must. It never lowers one, and it never raises one for size alone.

sensors._comment: The deterministic checks that run before any model review. A red sensor costs one review at the tier's model — today's price. A green one must therefore be impossible to fake: every ambiguity resolves to red, `unavailable` or `stale`, never to green. A missing lint_command is NOT green; only a human writing `lint_command: none` in testing.md makes it not_applicable. At or below skip_review_at_or_below, all green replaces the model review (risk-tiers.md, 'When the sensors replace the review'); a task over its diff budget never qualifies, whatever its sensors say. The `diff` sensor is red over the budget only when diff_budget.enforce is true; otherwise it reports the size and stays green.

escalation_triggers: the STRONG tier could not resolve an ambiguity and said so
two constraints in the architecture contradict each other
several viable high-risk designs remain and the choice is not reversible
the cost of being wrong is very high (money, data loss, legal or fiscal exposure)
escalation_rule: Start at the tier the table gives. Escalate one step, for one task, when a trigger fires — never escalate the whole pipeline, and never start at EXPERT because it exists. Never retry a failed reasoning task on a cheaper tier; downgrading is for mechanical work only.
downgrade_rule: A tier may be lowered only by a human, in writing, in the task record. An agent may propose a lower tier with evidence; it may not apply one.
remediation_rule: Failures are fixed in batches, never one at a time. A step's own scoped tests are the exception: they fail and are fixed inside that step. After the verification run, the e2e run (and after a review) collect every finding, classify each, open ONE `state.py remediate` step whose scope is the union of the finished steps plus the failing tests, fix them all, then run the verification command once more. A remediation never re-triages or re-plans the task; at most two rounds before the human decides.
